title: Finite biproduct equivalence for invertible curve assertions
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $k$ a field, $X$ a scheme and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.
Let $I$ be a finite index type and $G_a$ module sheaves on the small etale site of $X$.
Let $H$ be a module sheaf equipped with an isomorphism $e:H\simeq\bigoplus_a G_a$,
using finite biproducts [def-weil-additive-category]. The predicates $C_1,\ldots,C_8$
are those of [def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions], with their stated conditional hypotheses.
Let $r$ be prime and suppose $r\operatorname{id}_{G_a}=0$ for every $a$ and
$r\operatorname{id}_H=0$. Assume $G_a$ and $H$ constructible [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf].
Then $C_4(H)\land C_6(H)$ holds if and only if $C_4(G_a)\land C_6(G_a)$ holds for every $a$.
Invertible-order torsion has the stalk meaning of [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion].

source.place: Theorem 03SC, proof, fourth paragraph; Lemma 0A5C. Primary text checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03SC and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A5C.

proof.text: For any additive functor T to abelian groups, compose T.mapIso e, T.mapBiproduct G and AddCommGrpCat.biproductIsoPi to identify T(H) with the product of T(G a). The coordinate a is T(e.hom followed by biproduct.π G a). Each factor is a retract of T(H), hence injects into it; conversely a finite product of finite factors is finite. This gives finite_sum_iff, including the empty product. Apply it to forgetting coefficients followed by Sheaf.functorH in each degree.

Use Etale.cohomologyMap_map (the proved naturality lemma of the source library) to assemble pullback on cohomology into a natural transformation between the additive cohomology functors. Naturality with e.hom followed by each projection shows that under the two product identifications this map is the pointwise product of the component maps. Such a product map is bijective iff every component is: injectivity is tested using vectors supported at one coordinate; surjectivity in one coordinate follows by lifting such a vector; conversely choose preimages in every coordinate. The zero element supplies supported vectors, including the empty-family case. This is bijective_sum_iff and its cohomology specialization.

Split on whether r is a unit in Γ(Spec k, top). In the unit case prime_annihilated_invertible_cases supplies invertible-order torsion for H and every G a. Install the given constructibility hypotheses, and apply the preceding two equivalences degreewise and to each field-extension pullback square. Combine the resulting C4 and C6 proofs componentwise.

In the nonunit case, whenever the conditional invertible-order hypothesis on a prime-killed sheaf F is assumed, prime_annihilated_invertible_cases makes F zero. The additive coefficient-forgetting functor and inverse image preserve zero objects. Sheaf.subsingleton_H_of_isZero makes both source and target cohomology subsingletons. Source cohomology is finite, and pullback is injective and surjective (zero is a preimage). Thus both conditional assertions hold for H and each G a independently, completing both implications.

proof_origin.place: P2 Lean proof of the finite-sum argument in Stacks 03SC, fourth paragraph; prime-unit cases reused from lem-pbc-a3-prime-annihilated-invertible-cases. Generic biproduct and pointwise-map arguments proved privately in the item module.

lean.statement:
theorem prime_biproduct_invertible_iff (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ]
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (r : ℕ) [Fact r.Prime] {ι : Type} [Finite ι]
    (G : ι → Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ))
    (hGc : ∀ a, Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf (G a)) (hGr : ∀ a, r • 𝟙 (G a) = 0)
    {H : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)} (e : H ≅ ⨁ G)
    (hHr : r • 𝟙 H = 0)
    (hHc : Scheme.IsConstructibleSheaf H) :
    (FiniteOfInvertibleOrder Λ H k ∧ BaseChangeOfInvertibleOrder Λ f H) ↔
      ∀ a, FiniteOfInvertibleOrder Λ (G a) k ∧
        BaseChangeOfInvertibleOrder Λ f (G a)
